keyword: how long for artemis 2 to reach the moon

verifications.claim: Artemis II is scheduled to take approximately four days to reach the vicinity of the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'roughly a four-day journey to the far side of the moon'; R4: 'outbound trip of about four days'; R2: 'Days 5-6: Arrival at the moon'; R5: 'lunar observation four days and 22 hours into the mission'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state approximately four days from TLI or launch to moon vicinity.

verifications.claim: The crew will perform a lunar flyby on the sixth day of their mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Days 5-6: Arrival at the moon... on the sixth day'; R3: 'Closest approach April 6, 2026' (launch April 1); R5: 'furthest point a little more than five days'; R7: 'flyby... on April 6' (day 6)
verifications.reasoning: Sources consistently indicate flyby around day 6.

verifications.claim: The crew will reach a maximum distance of over 4,000 nautical miles above the lunar surface.
verifications.label: AMBIGUOUS
verifications.evidence: R2: 'at least 4,000 nautical miles above the moon’s surface'; R3: 'Distance 4,067 mi (6,545 km; 3,534 nmi)'
verifications.reasoning: R2 supports 'at least 4,000 nmi' pre-mission; R3 reports actual closest approach 3,534 nmi (under 4,000), creating contradiction between planned and actual.

verifications.claim: The entire mission will last about 10 days.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'about nine and a half days'; R3: '9 days, 1 hour'; R4: 'about 10 days'; R5: 'nearly 10-day... round up'; R6/R7: 'about 10 days'
verifications.reasoning: All sources describe mission as ~9.5-10 days.

verifications.claim: It takes about four days for the Orion spacecraft to travel from Earth to the far side of the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'roughly a four-day journey to the far side of the moon'; R4: 'outbound trip of about four days... around the backside of the Moon'
verifications.reasoning: Directly matches phrasing in sources for travel time to far side.

verifications.claim: The spacecraft will not enter orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'will not land on the moon or even go into lunar orbit'; R2: 'never entering low-lunar orbit'; R3: 'crewed lunar flyby... did not enter lunar orbit'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state no lunar orbit entry.

verifications.claim: The spacecraft will perform a "free-return trajectory" loop around the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'loop around it'; R3: 'free-return trajectory'; R4: 'lunar free return trajectory'; R5: 'free-return trajectory around the moon'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple direct mentions of free-return trajectory looping around Moon.

verifications.claim: The flyby will occur around day 6.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Days 5-6'; R3: 'April 6' (day 6); R5: '>5 days'; R7: 'today... April 6' (day 6)

verifications.claim: The crew is expected to return to Earth after a mission lasting roughly 9.5 to 10 days.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'nine and a half days'; R3: '9 days, 1 hour, 32 minutes'; R5: 'nine days, one hour and 46 minutes... 9.5 to 10 days'

verifications.claim: Artemis II is the first crewed mission to the Moon in over 50 years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first piloted moonshot since... 53 years ago'; R2: 'first manned mission... since Apollo 17 in 1972'; R3: 'first crewed flight beyond low Earth orbit since Apollo 17 in 1972'
verifications.reasoning: All confirm first crewed lunar mission since Apollo 17 (>50 years).

verifications.claim: Artemis II tests the Space Launch System (SLS) and Orion capsule with astronauts on board for future landing missions.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first with a crew on board — to make sure it's up to the task'; R3: 'test flight supporting subsequent Artemis missions aimed at returning humans to the lunar surface'; R4: 'confirm... systems... with crew aboard... for Artemis III and beyond'
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe as test of SLS/Orion with crew for future lunar landings.
